text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Truck drivers' strike and road blockades are starting to affect the economy, cost may offset the 0.9 percent GDP growth registered in the third quarter. Government may resort to decrees on working time and wages if negotiations fail. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).
-- Lagardere managing director Philippe Camus says in an interview says he is confident Thomson privatisation will go according to plan.
-- Credit Foncier de France expected to post up to one billion francs profit for 1996, and around 660 million francs for the first half, according to trade union sources.
-- Consortium de Realisation, a structure selling off Credit Lyonnais assets, to sell up to one billion francs real-estate loans portfolio.

-- Debate on mark-franc parity begins to affect the franc, which drew near 3.40 francs to a mark yesterday after Bank of France Monetary Policy Council member Jean-Pierre Gerard said a lower franc may be necessary because of German monetary policy.
-- Bouygues to rebuild waterfront in Beirut in contract estimated to be worth over 1.2 billion francs.
-- Bank of France Monetary Policy Council members divided over strong franc policy.
-- Siemens spokesman says hopes a planned merger between GEC Alsthom ALSF.CN and Framatome will not jeopardise its co-operation with Framatome on a European nuclear reactor project.
-- LVMH luxury groups buys 55 percent of vineyard Chateau d'Yquem for an estimated 500 million francs.
-- Truckers tighten grip on France, Britain may demand compensation for effects on trade.
